sections.title: JS-1: JavaScript Fundamentals — Part 2
sections.body:
# JS-1: JavaScript Fundamentals — Part 2

We have completed JavaScript runtime, variables, hoisting, scope, data types, memory management, operators, conditions, loops and array methods.

Now we will complete the remaining JavaScript fundamentals before moving to asynchronous JavaScript, which is particularly important for Playwright.

| Topic | Status |
|--------|--------|
| JavaScript runtime | Completed |
| Variables, scope and hoisting | Completed |
| Data types and memory | Completed |
| Operators and type coercion | Completed |
| Conditions and loops | Completed |
| Arrays and array methods | Completed |
| Objects and JSON | In progress |
| Destructuring, spread and rest | Upcoming |
| Functions and callbacks | Upcoming |
| Coding exercises and interview | Upcoming |

sections.title: Objects and JSON
Destructuring, spread and rest operators

quiz.question: What is the difference between a JavaScript object and JSON?
options: Interviewer: A JavaScript developer uses optional chaining everywhere.
Interviewer: Your application logs complete request objects.
Interviewer: An agent continuously calls the same tool without completing the user task.
An object is an in-memory data structure. JSON is a standardized textual representation used to exchange compatible data between systems.
quiz.explanation: An object is an in-memory data structure. JSON is a standardized textual representation used to exchange compatible data between systems.

quiz.question: What is the difference between JSON.parse and JSON.stringify?
options: Interviewer: Your JavaScript service processes one million retrieved document records using multiple array methods.
Interviewer: A JavaScript developer uses optional chaining everywhere.
Interviewer: Your application expects JSON, but the model returns malformed JSON or valid JSON with incorrect field types.
JSON.parse() converts JSON text into JavaScript values. JSON.stringify() serializes compatible JavaScript values into JSON text.
quiz.explanation: JSON.parse() converts JSON text into JavaScript values. JSON.stringify() serializes compatible JavaScript values into JSON text.

quiz.question: What happens to undefined during serialization?
options: Interviewer: Your application logs complete request objects.
Interviewer: Your application expects JSON, but the model returns malformed JSON or valid JSON with incorrect field types.
Interviewer: An agent continuously calls the same tool without completing the user task.
Undefined object properties are omitted, while undefined array elements are serialized as null.
quiz.explanation: Undefined object properties are omitted, while undefined array elements are serialized as null.

quiz.question: Can JSON.stringify serialize circular references?
options: Interviewer: Your application expects JSON, but the model returns malformed JSON or valid JSON with incorrect field types.
Interviewer: Your tests pass when executed individually but fail when running in parallel.
Interviewer: An agent continuously calls the same tool without completing the user task.
Not directly. It normally throws a TypeError.
quiz.explanation: Not directly. It normally throws a TypeError.

quiz.question: How do you ensure an LLM-generated JSON response is safe for tool execution?
options: Interviewer: Your tests pass when executed individually but fail when running in parallel.
Interviewer: An agent continuously calls the same tool without completing the user task.
Interviewer: Your application expects JSON, but the model returns malformed JSON or valid JSON with incorrect field types.
Parse the response, validate its schema, enforce business rules, verify tool authorization, check resource ownership and execute only within approved permissions.
quiz.explanation: Parse the response, validate its schema, enforce business rules, verify tool authorization, check resource ownership and execute only within approved permissions. These are frequently used in TypeScript, Playwright fixtures, API responses and agent state management.
